summary: fix(canvas): repair `which` discovery, bound MCP responses, de-duplicate primary-key extraction, cover credential resolution, surface silent mirror failures, drop inert scaffolding
reason: An architecture review of the printed CLI surfaced six defects and duplications in generator-owned files. Three were live user-facing bugs: `which` — the discovery command CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and SKILL.md all point agents at first — returned wrong or empty results for every query tried; the MCP server applied no size ceiling to tool results, returning 973,781 bytes for a 4,000-item list straight into an agent's context while 280 lines of working truncation logic sat unreachable; and local-mirror write failures were discarded at 400 call sites, leaving a broken store silently serving stale data. The rest were a duplicated primary-key rule across two packages, a security-critical credential resolver with zero tests, and generator scaffolding that never applied to Canvas. NOTE ON VERSION: this CLI was printed at 4.25.0 while the current generator is 4.30.1. Every finding was re-checked against the 4.30.1 templates before recording an upstream item. Two were already fixed upstream and are NOT deferred: MCP code-orchestration results are bounded via bound.EndpointResponse (mcp_code_orch.go.tmpl, landed with #3210), and which tokenizes command names with whichSubTokens rather than strings.Fields. Both local fixes are therefore superseded by a reprint rather than by an upstream change.
validated_outcome: go test ./... green across all 7 packages; go vet and gofmt clean; golangci-lint (with a v2-compatible config — see the canvas-golangci-config-version note) shows 739 findings against main's 743, with zero introduced by these changes. 30 tests added across which resolution, MCP response bounding, primary-key extraction, credential resolution and mirror-failure reporting. Every rule mutation-checked; two mutations initially survived and the tests were rewritten until they did not. internal/config went from zero tests to 13.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generated read commands should call resolveRead(...) rather than resolveReadWithStrategy(..., "auto", ...).
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Machine-level, and a one-line template change. All 524 generated read call sites pass the identical literal "auto", and resolveRead already exists as exactly that 9-parameter wrapper with zero callers. The strategy parameter is a seam with one adapter: it adds width to a 10-parameter interface without adding behaviour. This was deliberately NOT fixed locally — the local form is a 524-file diff that fixes no bug, enables no test, and is undone by the next print, while the template form fixes every printed CLI permanently. The transformation is mechanical: resolveReadWithStrategy(cmd.Context(), c, flags, "auto", -> resolveRead(cmd.Context(), c, flags,

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Do not emit API-shape helpers into printed CLIs whose spec cannot use them.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: internal/types shipped as an empty package. internal/cache shipped with zero importers, duplicating the file cache internal/client already implements inline. cliutil/odata_date.go, extractnumber.go and jwtshape.go cite Exact Online, Dynamics 365, Binance, Coinbase, Stripe and cookie-jar JWT scraping in their own doc comments — none apply to a bearer-token REST API. Emitting them costs every printed CLI dead weight and lint noise. Note the inverse mistake is also easy: cliutil/fanout.go and probe.go also had zero call sites but are tested, correct and plausibly useful here, so they were kept.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generated helpers should be wired to the shared implementation rather than reimplemented inline.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: client.go recomputed the 2^attempt retry curve inline while cliutil.Backoff sat unused implementing the same curve plus a MaxBackoff ceiling. The template emitted both the helper and a copy of its body.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: which scoring: score WhyItMatters, match the group tag by whole token, and tokenize descriptions with whichSubTokens. Filed as #4016. The command-tree fallback is #3370, commented with the hidden-area-group traversal detail.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Verified against 4.30.1, not just this 4.25.0 print. WhyItMatters is emitted into every index entry and never read by whichScoreEntry. The group tag is substring-matched at which.go.tmpl:153 while line 52 documents it as whole-word, which let the token 'at' match inside 'that' in an unrelated group label. Descriptions use strings.Fields while commands use whichSubTokens. The hyphen-tokenization defect this CLI exhibits is ALREADY FIXED upstream and is not part of the report.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Primary-key extraction should exist once. The generator emits it into both internal/store and internal/cli.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Machine-level. 86 of 105 non-comment lines were byte-identical across the two copies, five helper names shared verbatim, and both carried the same comment warning that 'divergence here produces silent drops on heterogeneous payloads'. internal/cli's copy had a single caller and now calls store.ExtractResourceID; equivalence was verified over 250 resource/payload combinations before deleting.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: writeMutationResponseToStore should not discard errors, and templates should give best-effort background work a way to report failure.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Machine-level. The template emits `if err != nil { return }` on open and `_, _, _ =` on the upsert, at 400 call sites per printed CLI. Because the function takes no writer, the local fix warns once per process to os.Stderr; a template-level fix could thread a writer through instead.
